title: Apply the rule
hook: Quoting “sort ascending” is easier than applying it to new values.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Use a stated sorting rule on a fresh set rather than repeat its wording.

objective: Use a stated sorting rule on a fresh set rather than repeat its wording.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Quoting “sort ascending” is easier than applying it to new values. What checks application of ascending order? Correct option: Order new values. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred.

claims.text: The target uses new values ordered smallest to largest. Matching the rule requires applying it to the numbers shown.
claims.source: Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science 17(3),249–255, DOI10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x; publisher abstract retrieved 2026-10-13: https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x/ . Prose-passage experiments found delayed retention advantages for retrieval over restudy. This short exercise does not establish that effect for the learner. Fixture mappings and rules are explicit conventions, not empirical demonstrations.

claims.text: The displayed match count compares the learner’s ordering of 2, 5, 9 with ascending order. The unsorted input stays visible while they work. There is no measured learning or productivity gain.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, apply-not-quote fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts. Stage rules: check reconstructed token positions against the covered target; count exact matches out of three. Application refinement presents new unsorted input 5, 9, 2 and leaves it visible while the learner rearranges the separate attempt row. No Cover control is offered; a real swap is required before checking. Feedback marks which attempt positions match ascending order 2, 5, 9 after Check; the unsorted input remains unchanged. This is a rule-application fixture, not a recall or retention test.

claims.text: Recall question answer and rationale: Order new values. The target uses new values ordered smallest to largest. Matching the rule requires applying it to the numbers shown.
